newsitem.title: CHINA: China says forex management system improved.
newsitem.headline: China says forex management system improved.

text.p: China's handling of foreign exchange has improved dramatically, resulting in simplified procedures and increased foreign exchange reserves, the Shanghai securities News reported on Sunday.

The paper quoted Zhou Xiaochuan, head of the State Foreign Exchange Manager Bureau, as saying the government's basic targets on reform of foreign exchange management had been met since the abolition in 1994 of the dual exchange rate.
"Since then, the heart of the reform work has been to construct an exchange rate mechanism which is based upon market forces," Zhou told a conference in Beijing.

"The reforms of the foreign exchange structure have to a very large extent worked to the benefit of importers and exporters. The current system is much simpler and more transparent than the foreign dual exchange rate system."
He added that China's foreign exchange reserves had grown sharply as a result of the reforms, and not simply as a result of China's trade surplus.
At the end of 1995, China's foreign exchange reserves were $73.6 billion, up from $51.7 billion at the end of 1994.
Zhou also expressed satisfaction with the strength of the yuan, which has risen to 8.3 to the U.S. dollar from 8.7 in early 1994 despite significant inflation over much of that period.
